title: Recent Release, "46," from Page Publishing Author Scott Douglas, Explores the Mothman Legend and Tragic 1966–67 Events in Point Pleasant, West Virginia
excerpt: Scott Douglas has completed a new book, titled, "46," a haunting narrative that reimagines one of America's most enigmatic cryptid encounters...
content:
Charleston, WV, November 25, 2026 --(PR.com)-- Scott Douglas has completed a new book, titled, "46," a haunting narrative that reimagines one of America's most enigmatic cryptid encounters through the eyes of the creature itself. Set against the backdrop of decaying TNT bunkers and winding roads in Point Pleasant, the story unfolds as a silent witness to ordinary lives teetering on the edge of catastrophe. With crimson eyes and wings that swallowed the darkness, the Mothman drifts above the fragile community, appearing in fleeting glimpses to lovers and unsuspecting people as an unwilling herald of doom.

Douglas, a native West Virginian and veteran of the United States Air Force, brings an intimate understanding of the region and its mysteries to his debut novel. As a small business owner turned published author, he channels his deep connection to West Virginia's folklore and history into this gripping work, crafting a narrative that transforms the legendary creature from mere speculation into a sentient observer of human tragedy. His firsthand knowledge of the landscape and culture grounds the fantastical premise in authentic regional detail.

"46" delves into themes of fate, helplessness, and the burden of foreknowledge as readers discover what truly transpired during those haunted months. The novel explores the tragedy surrounding the Silver Bridge collapse while weaving together the threads of the Mothman sightings into a cohesive, emotionally resonant tale. As the narrative unfolds toward its inevitable conclusion, readers will confront profound questions about destiny, warning, and the anguish of witnessing calamity without the power to prevent it.

"This story demanded to be told from a perspective nobody had considered before," said Douglas. "By inhabiting the consciousness of the Mothman itself, I wanted readers to experience the tragedy of Point Pleasant not as observers solving a mystery, but as participants in an ancient, sorrowful knowledge."
Published by Page Publishing, this atmospheric work offers readers an entirely fresh interpretation of a historical legend. The novel transforms a cryptozoological phenomenon into a meditation on fate and compassion, delivering both supernatural intrigue and profound human insight.

Readers who wish to experience this haunting work can purchase "46" at bookstores everywhere, or online at the Apple iTunes Store, Amazon, Google Play, or Barnes and Noble.
